content_voiceover: This is a dense summary table for Wilms tumor that fellows should memorize for boards. The primary site is almost always the kidney, and about eleven percent of cases are bilateral. Pathology shows the classic triphasic pattern, persistent blastema, dysplastic epithelial tubules, and supporting mesenchymal or stromal elements. The key genes are WT1 at eleven p one three and WT2 at eleven p fifteen point five. Prognostic factors include tumor stage, histology, where lack of anaplasia is favorable, age, where being younger than two years old with a small tumor under five hundred fifty grams and stage one favorable histology is a good sign, completeness of lung nodule response, and loss of heterozygosity at one p and sixteen q, which is unfavorable. Treatment involves nephrectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, and sometimes pre-operative chemotherapy is needed to shrink the tumor first. Two special treatment concerns to remember, never biopsy a stage one Wilms tumor because it can upgrade the stage, and radiotherapy should start within five to seven days after nephrectomy. Five-year overall survival is excellent, greater than ninety-five percent for stages one through three with favorable histology, and eighty-five percent overall.
keypoints: Kidney primary, eleven percent bilateral, classic triphasic histology
Key genes, WT1 at eleven p one three, WT2 at eleven p fifteen point five
Unfavorable factors, anaplasia and loss of heterozygosity at one p and sixteen q
Never biopsy stage one Wilms tumor, start radiotherapy within five to seven days post-nephrectomy
Five-year overall survival, greater than ninety-five percent for favorable stage one to three, eighty-five percent overall
keypoint_voiceover: Board pearls here, do not biopsy a suspected stage one Wilms tumor since that can upgrade its stage, and if radiotherapy is indicated it needs to start within five to seven days after nephrectomy. Favorable histology plus early stage carries an excellent prognosis, over ninety-five percent five-year survival, while anaplasia and loss of heterozygosity at one p and sixteen q push the tumor into an unfavorable category.
